[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Neural Network Construction in TensorFlow: Functional API and Subclassing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"While tf.keras.Sequential is ideal for stacking linear layers, real-world deep learning architectures often require non-linear topologies, shared layers, multiple inputs or outputs, and dynamic control flow. TensorFlow provides two advanced approaches for building these models: the Functional API and Model Subclassing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. The Keras Functional API"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Functional API allows you to build graphs of layers. It is well-suited for models with complex topologies, such as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), multi-input/multi-output models, and models with shared layers."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import tensorflow as tf

inputs = tf.keras.Input(shape=(32,))
x = tf.keras.layers.Dense(64, activation=\'relu\')(inputs)
x = tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.5)(x)
outputs = tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation=\'softmax\')(x)

functional_model = tf.keras.Model(inputs=inputs, outputs=outputs, name=\'functional_mlp\')
functional_model.summary()"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Explicit Input Definition: Uses tf.keras.Input to specify the tensor shape and data type."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Callable Layers: Layers are treated as functions that take tensors and return tensors."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Model Instantiation: Combines the designated inputs and outputs into a tf.keras.Model object."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Model Subclassing"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Model Subclassing is an object-oriented approach where you inherit from tf.keras.Model and write your own forward pass in the call method. This provides maximum flexibility for custom training loops and dynamic architectures."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"class SubclassedModel(tf.keras.Model):
    def __init__(self, num_classes=10):
        super(SubclassedModel, self).__init__()
        self.dense1 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(64, activation=\'relu\')
        self.dropout = tf.keras.layers.Dropout(0.5)
        self.dense2 = tf.keras.layers.Dense(num_classes, activation=\'softmax\')

    def call(self, inputs, training=False):
        x = self.dense1(inputs)
        x = self.dropout(x, training=training)
        return self.dense2(x)

subclassed_model = SubclassedModel(num_classes=10)"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"State Initialization: Layers are defined inside the __init__ constructor."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Imperative Forward Pass: Operations and routing logic are implemented inside the call method."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Dynamic Behavior: Easily incorporate conditional logic (e.g., if statements) during execution."},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Trade-offs"},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Functional API: Offers safety features like built-in validation, easy serialization, and plotting, but is limited to static graphs."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Subclassing: Provides ultimate flexibility for research and custom logic, but architecture is hidden inside the call method, making it harder to debug or serialize."}]
